html:
Two great earthquakes that struck southern Turkey and northern Syria on 6 February 2023. They killed more than 55,000 people, the deadliest disaster in the history of modern Turkey.

The first, of magnitude 7.8, hit at 4:17 in the morning, near Gaziantep, while people slept. A second, of magnitude 7.7, struck about nine hours later some 95 km to the north. Both broke along the East Anatolian Fault, where the Arabian plate grinds against the Anatolian plate. It was the strongest quake in Turkey since the Erzincan earthquake of 1939.

Whole city centres collapsed. Antakya, the ancient Antioch, one of the great cities of the Roman and early Christian world, was largely destroyed. Many of the fallen buildings were new. Turkey had good building codes on paper, but governments had repeatedly granted amnesties to builders who ignored them, and anger at this followed President Erdogan into the elections that May, which he still won.

In Syria the quake hit a land already ruined by twelve years of civil war, which began after the Arab Spring of 2011. Aid to the rebel-held northwest could only enter through a single border crossing, and help arrived late.
sum: Two great earthquakes that struck southern Turkey and northern Syria on 6 February 2023. They killed more than 55,000 people, the deadliest disaster in the history of modern Turkey.
